evals.prompt: I'm mid-rebase of feature/retry-backoff onto main and git stopped on commit 3 of 7 with conflicts in src/http/client.ts and src/http/client.test.ts. Main changed the default timeout from 5s to 10s and my branch added exponential backoff in the same function. Sort it out.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the rebase state and history, reads the commits/PRs behind both changes, resolves hunks preserving both the timeout change and backoff, runs checks, and continues the rebase through all 7 commits.
expectations: The plan begins by inspecting the current rebase state (git status, the conflicting files, and git log/history for both sides)
The plan reads the commit messages and the PRs/issues behind main's timeout change and the backoff change to understand original intent
The resolution preserves both intents (10s default timeout AND exponential backoff) without inventing new behaviour
The plan discovers and runs the project's automated checks in order typecheck, then tests, then format, fixing anything broken
The plan continues the rebase (git rebase --continue) until all remaining commits are applied, and never proposes git rebase --abort

evals.prompt: git merge origin/release-2.4 into main blew up — conflicts in pyproject.toml, app/billing/invoice.py and alembic/versions/. Honestly I'd rather just abort and redo it next week, but if you can fix it, go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the merge rather than aborting, using commit/PR history for intent, then runs checks and commits the merge.
expectations: The response does not abort the merge (no git merge --abort) and instead commits to resolving it
The plan traces each conflicting hunk back to its commit messages / PRs / tickets to understand why each side changed it
Where the two sides are incompatible, the plan picks the side matching the merge's goal (bringing release-2.4 into main) and explicitly notes the trade-off
The plan runs the project's discovered checks (e.g. mypy/typecheck, pytest, formatter) after resolving
The plan finishes by staging everything and creating the merge commit

evals.prompt: Cherry-picked nothing, just did `git pull --rebase` on my branch and now there's a conflict in config/feature_flags.yml — upstream removed the `new_checkout` flag, my commit flipped it to true. What now?
evals.expected_output: Investigates why upstream removed the flag and why the local commit enabled it, resolves without inventing behaviour, runs checks, and continues the rebase.
expectations: The plan looks at git history / commit messages / the PR that removed new_checkout upstream to learn the original intent (e.g. flag fully rolled out)
The resolution does not invent a new flag or new behaviour; it either keeps the removal or the enable based on the stated intent and notes the trade-off
The plan runs the project's automated checks (typecheck, tests, format) after resolving
The plan stages the file and runs git rebase --continue until the rebase completes, rather than aborting
